message.reasoning:
I'm planning a two-minute drum script at 110 BPM using deterministic seeded randomness, structuring events by time, note, velocity, and limb assignment (right hand, left hand, kick, hihat pedal) while making sure limb usage stays physically plausible.

I'm sketching the arrangement into sections—intro, main groove, Latin percussion variation, build, breakdown, climax, and return/ending—along with a repeating 16th-note motif that gets displaced and reorchestrated across toms and percussion. Now I'm writing a helper function to add each note event with its bar, step, pitch, velocity, and limb.

Setting up swing timing with delayed offbeat 16ths, laid-back snare, pushed ride, and small deterministic velocity variation, plus a dictionary keyed by tick and limb to avoid overlapping hits on the same hand. Writing MIDI export logic...

Mapping out the full GM drum note numbers for cowbell, timbales, congas, claves, and other percussion, then sketching a one-bar motif with kick and crash on the downbeat, snare accents, and tom fills near the end of the bar.

Now I'm designing groove and fill functions with cymbal patterns, ghost-note snare probability, motif overlays, and descending tom fills, plus timing logic with swing offsets and per-limb humanization. Writing timing and swing code...

For the ending, I'm calculating that 55 bars at 110 BPM gives exactly 120 seconds, with the final big hit landing around bar 54 followed by a ringing tail to close out the piece.
